info.name: TRICC OpenSRP → FHIR Push
info.description:
Postman equivalent of push-to-fhir.sh (copied into the OpenSRPStrategy export package next to it).

Workflow:
1. Run "Get Access Token" (skip if your server has SKIP_AUTH=1 / uses a HAPI server with no auth — in that case just remove the Authorization header from the upload requests).
2. For each exported JSON file under the package (questionnaire/, plan-definition/, library/, structure-map/, value-set/, composition/, …), open "PUT Resource (template)", set the `resourceType` and `resourceId` variables to the resource's own `resourceType`/`id` fields (NOT the filename), paste the file contents as the raw body, and Send.
3. Upload every resource type before Composition — gateways often require the referenced resources (Questionnaire, PlanDefinition, Library, StructureMap, ValueSet, Binary, …) to exist before the Composition that lists them.

Postman collections can't walk a local directory tree, so this does not loop over files automatically the way push-to-fhir.sh does — use the Collection Runner with a data file (one row per {resourceType, resourceId, file} ) if you want to batch it, or fall back to the shell script for bulk pushes.

request.description: Equivalent of the KEYCLOAK_* password-grant call in push-to-fhir.sh. Skip this request entirely if you already have a token (set FHIR_ACCESS_TOKEN directly) or the target server has SKIP_AUTH=1.

Set resourceType/resourceId to match the JSON body's own `resourceType`/`id` fields (never the filename — see push-to-fhir.sh's read_fhir_meta) and replace the body with the exported resource JSON. Duplicate this request per file, or drive it from the Collection Runner with a data file of {resourceType, resourceId, file} rows. Remove the Authorization header if SKIP_AUTH=1 / talking to an open HAPI server.

push-to-fhir.sh always uploads Composition resources last, since gateway ACLs typically require the resources a Composition references to already exist. Send this only after every other resource in the package has been PUT successfully.
